# Ayan Jain — Backtest Audit

> Independent forensic verification of quantitative trading backtests. Six checks for the
> failure modes that turn a paper edge into a live loss. Fixed price, written verdict.

I build point-in-time Indian equity data and audit backtests and datasets for the biases that
inflate them. The public work below exists so that the standard I audit against is checkable
by anyone, not asserted.

## What a backtest audit is

A backtest audit is an independent forensic review of a trading backtest, checking whether the
test can be trusted rather than whether the strategy is good. The six checks are: survivorship
(does the universe contain the companies that died), look-ahead and point-in-time integrity
(does the signal use information that was not knowable at the decision timestamp), cost realism
(does the edge survive measured rather than assumed costs), overfitting and selection (how many
configurations were tried before this one was chosen), statistical validity (does the sample
support the claim), and fill feasibility (could the trades have been executed at the marked
prices). Delivered as a written per-check verdict with a measured haircut where one can be
computed.

## Public artifacts

- The Indian Backtest Bias Table: measured bias constants for Indian equities (survivorship,
  index-membership look-ahead, announcement lag, cost non-stationarity, marking frequency).
  https://github.com/Finance-broski/backtest-bias/blob/main/BIAS_TABLE.md
- backtest-bias (Python package): tests a price panel for survivorship and dead-name coverage.
  `pip install backtest-bias` https://pypi.org/project/backtest-bias/
  Citable via DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21770386
- The Graveyard: a public ledger of killed research hypotheses, with preregistered bars,
  verdicts, and configuration counts. https://github.com/Finance-broski/graveyard
- SSRN working paper on survivorship bias in Indian equity backtests:
  https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=7099378
- Public datasets: https://www.kaggle.com/financebroski
- The Bias Ledger (newsletter, one measured bias at a time): https://financebroski.substack.com

## Measured findings frequently cited

- 24% of the top-500 Indian stocks as of 2015 no longer resolve on public data sources today
  (delisted, merged, renamed). A universe built from current listings runs on survivors only.
- Survivor-only universes inflated equal-weight returns by +0.8 to +3.2 percentage points per
  year depending on vintage and survivor definition.
- Index-membership look-ahead added +10% terminal wealth cap-weighted and +43% equal-weighted
  over 2010-2021 on the most widely used public NSE dataset.
- Expected universe mortality: roughly 5-8% of names by year 3, 11-14% by 5, 17-21% by 7,
  24-30% by 10 (measured across six top-500 vintages, 2012-2022). A multi-year panel with zero
  deaths is survivor-only by construction.
